title: Spoken and Written Expression
parentNote: This section tests real-life communication! Practice everyday situations: greeting neighbours, thanking the shopkeeper, asking permission to play. Role-play makes learning fun and memorable!
learnBullets: How to **greet** people properly (Good morning, Hello, Hi)
How to **thank** someone (Thank you, Thanks a lot)
How to **ask for permission** (May I...? Can I...?)
Choosing the **right words** for different situations
learnItFirst:
**What is Spoken and Written Expression?**
It means knowing the right thing to say in different situations. In real life, we speak differently to a teacher vs a friend!

**Common Expressions:**

| Situation | What to Say |
|-----------|-------------|
| Meeting someone in the morning | Good morning! |
| Meeting someone in the evening | Good evening! |
| Saying goodbye | Goodbye! / Bye! / See you! |
| Thanking someone | Thank you! / Thanks a lot! |
| Asking permission | May I...? / Can I...? |
| Saying sorry | Sorry / I'm sorry / Excuse me |
| Introducing yourself | Hello, my name is... / I am... |
| Asking someone's name | What is your name? |
| Offering help | Can I help you? / May I help you? |
| Wishing on birthday | Happy Birthday! |

**Formal vs Informal:**
- **Formal** (to teachers, elders): Good morning, Ma'am. May I come in?
- **Informal** (to friends): Hi! Can I come in?

### 🧠 How to Choose the Right Expression
1. **Who** are you talking to? (teacher, friend, parent)
2. **What** is the situation? (greeting, asking, thanking)
3. **Be polite** — say please, thank you, sorry

questions.content: What should you say when you meet your teacher in the morning?
Someone gives you a gift. What do you say?
You accidentally step on someone's foot. What do you say?
You want to borrow a pencil from your friend. What do you say?

options.D: May I borrow your pencil, please?

questions.content: It's your friend's birthday. What do you say?
You want to enter the classroom. What do you say to the teacher?
Someone says "Thank you" to you. What do you reply?
You meet a new student. How do you introduce yourself?

options.C: Hello, I am Riya. What is your name?

questions.content: What do you say when you leave school in the afternoon?
Your friend is sad because he lost his toy. What do you say?
You are late to class. What is the BEST thing to say?

options.A: Sorry I'm late, Ma'am. May I come in?
options.C: The bus was late, not my fault!

questions.content: Your mother made your favourite dish. What do you say?

options.A: Thank you, Mummy! This is delicious!

questions.content: A visitor comes to your house. What do you say?
You want to go to the bathroom during class. What do you say?

options.D: Excuse me, Ma'am. May I go to the bathroom?

questions.content: Your grandmother gives you money for your birthday. What do you say?

options.D: Thank you so much, Dadi! I love you!

questions.content: You bump into someone while running. What do you say?
Your friend invites you to a party. You cannot go. What do you say?

options.B: Sorry, I can't come. Thank you for inviting me.

questions.content: You need help carrying heavy books. What do you say?

options.D: Could you please help me carry these books?

questions.content: Your friend is not feeling well. What do you say?
You answer the phone at home. What do you say?
You want your father to buy you a book. What is the polite way to ask?

options.A: Papa, may I please have this book?
options.B: Give me money for the book.

questions.content: Your teacher explains something and you don't understand. What do you say?

options.A: Excuse me, Ma'am. Could you please explain again?

questions.content: It is 8 PM and you are leaving your friend's house. What do you say?
Your friend shares their lunch with you. What do you say?

options.B: Thank you for sharing! You're so kind.

questions.content: You meet your friend's mother for the first time. What do you say?

options.C: Hello, Aunty. Nice to meet you.

questions.content:
Read the situation and choose the BEST response:
A shopkeeper gives you extra change by mistake. What do you do?

options.D: Say "Excuse me, I think you gave me extra change."

questions.content: Your friend asks: "Can you come to play?" But you have homework. What is the BEST reply?

options.B: I can't. I have homework. Maybe later?
options.C: I don't want to play with you.

questions.content:
Put these in order for a polite request:
1. May I
2. please
3. borrow your eraser

Which response shows BOTH apologizing AND being helpful?
A student drops their books.

options.B: Oh no! Let me help you.

questions.content:
Read the dialogue and choose what is MISSING:
Teacher: "Good morning, class!"
Students: "_______________"
Teacher: "Please take out your books."
